newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Prudential NZ balanced funds up 11 pct-plus in '96.
newsitem.headline: Prudential NZ balanced funds up 11 pct-plus in '96.

text.p: Prudential's large balanced funds produced gross returns ranging upwards from about 11 percent during 1996, thanks to stronger economic confidence in the second half of last year, the company said on Tuesday.
It said balanced or diversified funds make up more than half of the NZ$1.1 billion under management by the group's investment arm, Prudential Portfolio Managers.
Total funds under management and service topped $1 billion for the first time last year.

The Prudential Personal Superannuation balanced fund produced a one-year return of 10.39 percent before tax and management fees, while the balanced fund's two-year return to the end of 1996 was 13.24 percent compounded annually.
The five-year compound annual rate was 11.95 percent, including re-investment of returns.
The Personal Superannuation entrepreneurial fund returned 12.76 percent over one year, 14.05 percent over two years and 13.65 percent annually over the past five years.

Prudential said its international superannuation funds continued to be among the top performers in New Zealand-based global equity funds. The international growth fund earned 13.17 percent gross last year (10.77 percent over two years).
The international balanced fund returned 12.53 percent in 1996 and 12.79 percent annually over the past two years (neither fund has operated for more than two years).
Prudential Portfolio Managers NZ Ltd managing director Greg Whitten said the outlook for 1997 was encouraging.

"Internationally, the American and European economies are likely to produce economic growth somewhere near long-term trends of 2.5 percent without significant fear of inflation igniting. Around the world, shares are preferred to fixed income investments," he said.

"Here in New Zealand, for the first time since 1991, both monetary and fiscal stimulation are occurring concurrently. The economy is still slowing and first quarter of 1997 may prove to be the low point in this cycle.
"The outlook is for a significant pick-up in economic growth during 1997 and into 1998."
"The medium-term outlook is most encouraging and should provide an environment in which New Zealanders can save and invest with confidence."
